articles.title: CIA-Mossad In Iran? Tehran Claims US-Israeli Links Behind January 'Coup Attempt' Protest
articles.description: Iran has announced a fresh intelligence crackdown following the violent unrest that erupted across the country in January. Iran's Intelligence Ministry says 30 alleged ringleaders, associates and vandals have been identified and arrested in Markazi Province. Iranian authorities accuse the suspects of being US- and Israel-backed operatives involved in attacks on homes, banks, government buildings, vehicles, shops, railway infrastructure and mosques. Tehran also claims weapons, alcohol and drugs were seized during the arrests. The arrests come amid Iran's long-running accusations against Israel's Mossad and the CIA, with Tehran repeatedly alleging that foreign intelligence agencies seek to exploit domestic unrest and destabilize the Islamic Republic. Iranian officials have described the January unrest as part of a US-Israeli-backed operation and say those responsible will face prosecution without a statute of limitations.

articles.title: Saudi, Turkey, Now Kuwait: Inside Pakistan's Growing Web Of Gulf Military Ties An Alarm For India?
articles.description: Pakistan has signed a new defence protocol with Kuwait, expanding cooperation in military training, capacity building and border management. The agreement builds on the 2023 Defence Cooperation Agreement and was signed in Islamabad by Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif and Kuwait’s Defence Minister Sheikh Abdullah Al-Salem Al-Sabah. The Kuwaiti delegation also met Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir. The deal follows Pakistan’s stronger mutual-defence pact with Saudi Arabia and its growing military relationship with Türkiye. This is not an automatic Kuwait–Pakistan war alliance, and there is no evidence that Kuwait has joined an anti-India bloc. But the agreement increases Pakistan’s role as a Gulf security partner. For India, the issue is the cumulative effect on defence influence, energy security, diaspora interests and regional diplomacy. Is Pakistan exporting military expertise to gain strategic relevance beyond its economic limitations?

articles.title: Quote of the day by Khalil Gibran, 'If you reveal your secrets to the wind, you should not blame the wind for revealing them to the trees' teaches powerful timeless wisdom about secrets, trust and consequences of sharing, shows psychology of maturity, mindset, healthy habits
articles.description: Quote of the day by Khalil Gibran remains memorable because it turns a complicated lesson about communication into a vivid natural metaphor. Words may begin as private thoughts, but once released, they can travel in unexpected directions. The modern world has only amplified that reality. Whether through face-to-face conversations or digital platforms, people should recognize that information can move quickly and sometimes permanently. Gibran’s quote invites us to pause before revealing what we would regret seeing repeated. Trust others, but also exercise judgment; value openness, but respect privacy; and most importantly, understand that the best way to protect a secret is to think carefully before sending it into the wind.
